spots.name: Mamutik
spots.desc: Island is also rather underdeveloped but is still accessible by jetty. Basic amenities like public toilet and shower are available. Chalets can be arranged with Sabah Parks if you don't wish to camp. This little island of slightly bigger than a football field is very diver friendly as it's ideal for shore dives, but due to the influx of the tourist hordes to this island, the shallow coral areas…

spots.name: Manukan
spots.desc: One of the most developed islands in the Tunku Abdul Rahman Marine Park due to its 1-km stretch of white sandy beach and pine-tree lined shores. Sutera Sanctuary Lodges have expensive beach and hill-side chalets here for rent, as well as a covered restaurant and a daily beach BBQ buffet spread. Other facilities include a snorkelling equipment rental hut, a small sundry shop, changing rooms.…

spots.name: Sapi
spots.desc: It's like Manukan, but smaller and is the second most developed island in the park. It has basic restaurant facilities, toilets (filthy), and snorkelling equipment rental. The Shangri-La hotel resort have their own staff and private beach over on the right of the jetty. There's a jungle trail around the island, and shallow water snorkelling offers some excitement. Where there was coral it has…

spots.name: Gaya Island
spots.desc: The largest of the islands by far. Has undergone some development on its northern shores, and has 2 exclusive resorts. Sabah Parks headquarters are further to the south-western, unspoiled part of Gaya island. Sabah Parks HQ and Downbelow Marine & Wildlife Adventures are set in a secluded bay with diving, snorkelling, jungle trekking, wildlife spotting and team building facilities. Gaya has a…

spots.name: Orchid Garden
spots.desc: The Orchid garden was opened in 1986. 700-800 species of orchids can be seen here. Malaysia has 3000 species altogether. There is a souvenir shop on the premises.

spots.name: Laman Selera MADANI Tanglin
spots.desc: Food court with Malay cuisine like nasi lemak, and nasi campur.

spots.name: Broga Hill Park
spots.desc: Hiking adventure. From Broga Hill peak to Tok Wan Mountain peak (675 meter).

spots.name: Jungle Railway Station
spots.desc: Gua Musang is a railway town: Once, trains were the only means of transport to the town. The journey provides a glimpse of village life in the jungle hinterland.

spots.name: Muse Ecopark
spots.desc: Set just below Gua Musang, the Ecopark allows use of their pool for 12RM for the day and has a via ferrata climbing the cliff before taking a flying fox back to the entrance (RM50). They also take guided tours up to the top of Gua Musang (RM35).

spots.name: Clock Tower
spots.desc: The central point of Fraser's Hill, this exceedingly British-looking little stone building covered with creeper vines is the most popular place to get your picture taken. The clock tower was designed by Malaysian Landscape Architect Z. Jaal and built by the Frasers Hill Development Corporation in 1989.

spots.name: Food Garden
spots.desc: This is actually just a small cluster of hawker stalls serving up cheap and tasty, if somewhat flyblown, local food. Most meals under RM5, but prices may add up if you order off the menu.

spots.name: Hillview Restaurant
spots.desc: serves Chinese and Western food. Tasty and relatively good value; Chinese meal for four at RM60. Serves excellent hot soup which is perfect for such cold weather.

spots.name: Smokehouse Restaurant
spots.desc: An expensive place for a western food but well worth a visit. A ribeye steak costs about RM55. There is a corkage charge of RM40 if you decide to BYO.

spots.name: Old Town
spots.desc: The main street Jalan Besar, with many old Chinese houses and street art.

spots.name: Wildlife
spots.desc: Dusky Langurs and Long Tailed Macaws will be in the jungle next to the road if you have a bit of a walk around the hills near dusk.

spots.name: Abandoned Colonial Buildings
spots.desc: Old abandoned buildings are scattered all through the town and on the hills around, such as Rest House Bukit Residen on the hill behind the Lipis Plaza Hotel, the old clubhouse next to the hospital and the district guest house up near the zoo.

spots.name: Railway Bridge
spots.desc: There is also a nice view of the train bridge if you go up Jalan Hospital to Jalan Orang Kaya Haji and you can follow the road/tracks around to view the kampung.

spots.name: Mosque
spots.desc: The wooden mosque Masjid Jln Masjid Lama, 100 m from the train station.

spots.name: Sidang Kopi
spots.desc: Charming little cafe next to the river with nice coffee and cakes

spots.name: Wong Yeong Moon Cake
spots.desc: They make Mooncake during the Autumn season. Other time, it runs as a Noodle Factory making noodles in the traditional style. Before arriving to the Noodle Factory, you can also visit the Tofu Factory (walking distance) Bukit Koman is a very small village and ask any villagers that you want to go to the Tofu Factory, you will be shown the way. The actual location is call "for char lu boi" it…

spots.name: Downtown
spots.desc: The centre of Kuala Besut is worth taking at least a quick look at, with colorful murals and old-looking wooden buildings. There's also an interesting Islamic cemetery that you'll see if you walk from the bus station to the jetty.

spots.name: Pantai Timor
spots.desc: A well sorted 2-floor supermarket near the Kuala Besut bus station and the market square. But they're not selling any alcoholic drinks.

spots.name: 7-Eleven
spots.desc: If you still need sunscreen, toothpaste or a charger this is the place to get it.

spots.name: Hua Guo Shan Temple
spots.desc: Temple with many monkeys running around. Free admission. There is also a stall that does fortune-telling based on your birthdate.

spots.name: Kelapa Sawit Wall Art
spots.desc: This short street alley has various beautiful murals painted on the walls.

spots.name: X Cafe D.I.Y Workshop
spots.desc: D.I.Y on pancake, beads key chain, earrings, handicraft, ice cream pocky, cooking pop set, cupcake & biscuit.

spots.name: Nasi Lemak Wat Kentut KTM Kulai
spots.desc: This shop sells nasi lemak with crispy fried chicken. The flagship shop is located about 1.5 km down the main road with the same name (Nasi Lemak Wat Kentut).

spots.name: 13th Month Restaurant & Cafe
spots.desc: Cafe with modern design specialized in pasta and suitable for vegetarian.

spots.name: Promised Garden
spots.desc: Outdoor dining cafe with garden theme and event space, built with reused materials.

spots.name: Klias Wetlands
spots.desc: The Klias Wetlands is a mangrove forest reserve along the Klias River. You will be able to see proboscis monkeys, long tail macaques, birds and fireflies. The best way to enjoy the wetlands is by a river cruise on the Klias River. Visit directly or join a tour group from Kota Kinabalu.

spots.name: Pulau Tiga Marine Park
spots.desc: One of the most unique islands in Malaysia, the Pulau Tiga Marine Park shot to fame for being the location of the first season of the reality-TV series "Survivor". The park covers an area of 15,864ha and includes three islands - Pulau Tiga, Kalampunian Besar and Kalampunian Damit. Pulau Tiga is unique for its mud volcanoes, the only ones found in Malaysia. The other Kalampunian Damit is also…

spots.name: Kundasang War Memorial
spots.desc: This tranquil garden memorial was established by a New Zealander in 1962. It was one of the foundation memorials to commemorate the tragic loss of Allied (mostly Australian and also British) POWs who died in 1945 during the infamous death marches from Sandakan to Ranau. Furthermore, it commemorates the brave Sabahan people who, at grave risk to their own lives, tried to help the dying POWs. The…

spots.name: Mesilau Park
spots.desc: It is on the slopes of Mount Kinabalu, accessible by a tarred road from Kundasang. They conduct guided 40-minute walks through a protected area which abounds with pitcher plants and orchids at 7AM and 11am, and sometimes in the afternoon too. The morning walk is best for seeing wildlife. It is also possible to climb the initial section of the route up Mount Kinabalu, or to walk the whole way to…

spots.name: Sabah Tea Garden
spots.desc: Offers light refreshments and meals overlooking the valley and mountain. Tours of the tea factory and gardens are offered. There is accommodation available in longhouse-style facilities. Although the tea is marketed as organic, realistically it is a very small section that is organic, and as it is grown alongside non-organic plants, cannot really be considered to be truly organic. It is a decent…

spots.name: Rainforest Discovery Centre
spots.desc: An environmental education centre situated within the Kabili-Sepilok Forest Reserve. Its primary function is to create public awareness and appreciation of the importance of conserving forests, as well as the sustainable use of forest resources. RDC has a 347 m-long canopy walkway strung between huge towers that allows great views of the forest canopy and is also good for bird-watchers.
spots.price: Adults RM 20, children 5-17 years old RM 7

spots.name: Taman Hiburan Jalil Alip Theme Park
spots.desc: A local recreation park popular among locals, to fish, paddle boats and feed local species of deer and crocodiles in their individual sanctuaries in the park.

spots.name: Kabili Trail
spots.desc: An 8km (16km round trip) hike to see the mangroves. The turnaround point is at the Sepilok Laut Reception Centre. This is a good spot to have lunch, but bring your own food and drink, because there is none to be found along the trip. There are several shelters with benches along the hike.
spots.price: RM15 on top of the RDC entrance fee, pay at the ticketing counter

spots.name: Kantin Sepilok
spots.desc: Located on the territory of the Forest Research Centre and caters mainly for its workers, however, anyone from outside can eat there as well. The menu is rather limited, usually they have only couple of options available at one time, most often they have rojak and chicken soup, also fried bananas and some snacks. Food is very tasty.

spots.name: Lepak Lounge
spots.desc: As long as it's located inside of the Rainforest Discovery Centre, anyone wishing to dine here needs to buy entrance ticket to RDC. There are always 5-6 types of meals available, such as chicken soup, fried rice, and fried chicken. The food is good, the service is fast.

spots.name: Cafeteria
spots.desc: Serves simple food like fried rice. It also has a small shop inside selling snacks, fruits, drinks. This place can get very busy at lunchtime as tour groups finish at the conservation centres.

spots.name: White House Bistro
spots.desc: Restaurant serves meat, but they speak English and understand vegan. They have a vegetarian menu, most of which is or can be made vegan. Near the Rainforest Discover Centre
spots.addr: Unnamed Road, Sepilok, 90000, Sabah (at Jalam fabia), Sandakan, Malaysia, 90000

spots.name: Borneo Sepilok Rainforest Resort
spots.desc: Restaurant at the resort has a separate vegan menu with options including tofu

spots.name: Labuk Bay Proboscis Monkey Sanctuary
spots.desc: Tours which take in Sepilok Orangutan Sanctuary often also visit the nearby Labuk Bay Proboscis Monkey Sanctuary. It is possible to drive there by Grab. The drivers propose that they wait for a long time for return, but for a higher price. Organizing a return trip by own for Grab or taxi involves a long wait. It is also possible to drive by car in the park, which is recommended due to the long…

spots.name: Sulug
spots.desc: The least developed of the isles with no facilities whatsoever, visitors can opt to camp if they wish to stay overnight. The island is inhabited and dive operators have daily trips there for diving off the corals on the northern shore as it is one of the best site around in Tunku Abdul Rahman Marine Park.

spots.name: Marine Ecology Research Center
spots.desc: The program focuses on Giant Clam propagation and coral restoration. The Marine Biologists at the center offers insights to visitors to help create awareness on the importance of taking care of the environment. It is open to the public for day trip visits.

spots.name: Borneo Dream
spots.desc: A boat transfer service is available to Tunku Abdul Rahman Marine Park for snorkelling or diving trips. Over 20 sites for diving and protected areas for snorkelling. Suitable for day trips. Goes to four of the main wreck dive sites on a regular basis. PADI Dive Boat, 10mx4m catamaran and a 9mx3m RIB, SDI resort dive centre, BSAC diver training centre, TDI resort dive centre and IANTD facility.…
spots.addr: F-G-1 Plaza Tanjung Aru, Jl. Mat Salleh

spots.name: Downbelow Marine & Wildlife Adventures
spots.desc: PADI 5 Star IDC Dive & Adventures Centre, PADI enriched air Nitrox diver courses. Offer structured and guided snorkelling, sea kayaking and trekking. Can accommodate very large groups for team building events and adventure training. Camping ground nearby with basic toilets and showers for guests. 3 dive boats, 37ft, 35ft & 32ft. Programs include a free pick up from Kota Kinabalu city hotels

spots.name: Pulau Lakei
spots.desc: This small island has a superb white sand beach. The National Parks Department has a small guard house located on the island. Trips to the island can be arranged with your boatman. There are some mysterious rock paintings just a short walk from the beach

spots.name: Paku trail
spots.desc: has the distinct advantage of being both relatively short and flat and offering one of the best opportunities to see the park's wildlife. It finishes at an attractive beach; one of the colonies of proboscis monkeys lives on the headland above

spots.name: Tajor trail
spots.desc: takes the visitor through varied terrain, including hilltops with extensive views, before finishing at a small but attractive waterfall, with calm pools that are safe for swimming in

spots.name: Limau trail
spots.desc: Continuing onwards from the Tajor trail, the park's longest and most arduous trek ends on a beach, though by the time you've scrambled down to it, it may be too late to enjoy; it's possible to arrange to be picked up by boat from the beach to save your weary legs further punishment; ask the boatmen at the jetty if they could pick you up at Limau beach because sometimes the sea is too rough for…

spots.name: Lintang trail
spots.desc: A circular loop taking the trekker through all the park's types of vegetation in half a day. Nice sightseeing.

spots.name: Kecil trail
spots.desc: A one and a half hour trek which ascends the forested hills overlooking Telok Assam, reaching a plateau covered in scrub vegetation, and continues along a sandy path lined with carnivorous pitcher plants, before reaching a cliff top with stunning views of the secluded bay below and the famous sea stack just offshore. A 10 minute descent through cliff vegetation brings you to one of the best…

spots.name: Kuala Kedah Fort
spots.desc: This fort is also known as the main gate of Kuala Kedah. It was built on 1771 by Sultan Abdullah and was completed in 1780. In 1821 it was conquered by the Siamese till 1842. Kota Kuala Bahang or Kota Kuala Kedah was no longer a battlefield after this time.

spots.name: Kulim Hi-Tech Park
spots.desc: 8 km from Kulim Town. It was the first integrated Hi-tech Park in Malaysia. The main activities at this park are jogging and cycling whilst enjoying the breathtaking wonders of the landscape. There are also facilities like pedestrian walks, gazebos, benches and a children’s playground.

spots.name: Junjung Waterfall
spots.desc: In Junjung, the waterfall is about 14 km from Kulim Town. Famous picnic place among locals.

spots.name: Sungai Sedim Recreational Forest
spots.desc: Sungai Sedim with its fast currents and rapids along with a forest ecosystem is the best place for exciting recreational activities. The main activities here include kayaking and white water rafting.

spots.name: Ulu Paip RainForest
spots.desc: In the Forest Reserves of Mount Bungsu with rapid river and forest ecosystem surroundings. The main activities here include picnicking, dipping, swimming and camping.

spots.name: Kulim Lake Garden
spots.desc: Putra Lake is the result of tin mining that was carried out in the area, as early as the 1850s. Visitors come here to either jog or take a walk on the pedestrian walk around the lake.

spots.name: Paya Besar
spots.desc: This suburb of Kulim is famously known as the 'Little India of Kulim'. There are many Indian fashion stores here, which sell mostly sarees, silk and cotton, almost anything that has the essence of India. Traditional costumes, spices, precious gold and costume jewelry which use semi-precious gems are widely sold by the most of the shops.

spots.name: Church of the Sacred Heart of Jesus
spots.desc: Famous and biggest Roman Catholic parish church in Kulim. The church in was established in 1948.

spots.name: Merdeka Clock Tower
spots.desc: The main landmark in Kulim. Ground breaking for the Merdeka Clock Tower was officiated by the late Tunku Abdul Rahman Putra, who was then the Chief Minister of the Federated States of Malaya, on 14 June 1957.

spots.name: Nattukkotai Nagaraththar Sri Thandayuthapani Temple
spots.desc: This is the temple of the Chettiar community in the town. The patron deity of the temple is Murugan, the deity associated with the Hindu festival of Thaipusam.

spots.name: The Hornbill Restaurant & Cafe
spots.desc: Nice restaurant. The terrace of the restaurant faces the bird park. So even without paying the entrance fee to the bird park it is possible to observe some of the animals.

spots.name: Rebung
spots.desc: Malay all-you-can-eat buffet. Four sessions per day: Breakfast, lunch, hi-tea, dinner. Very good online ratings.

spots.name: Nilai 3 Shopping Centre
spots.desc: You will find Textile and carpet wholesalers and manufacturers.

spots.name: Air Itam Dam
spots.desc: This was the first dam to be built on the island and is popular with locals as a picnic spot and jogging. The views of George Town at the crest of the dam are spectacular and rival Penang Hill. To reach the Dam you will require your own form of transport. Many locals walk or cycle up to the dam, taking around 40 minutes on foot from the Air Itam town centre.

spots.name: Jade Emperor's Pavilion
spots.desc: A Taoist temple located near the foot of Penang Hill dedicated to the Jade Emperor, one of the most important figures in Taoism. The current temple dates back to 1905, with a former temple existing on the grounds since 1869. The temple underwent restoration in 2002. During the Jade Emperor's Birthday, the 9th day of Chinese New Year, throngs of pilgrims come to visit and pray here.

spots.name: Kek Lok Si Temple
spots.desc: An impressive and expansive hillside temple complex, reputed to be the largest Buddhist temple in South-east Asia. Much of the temple is free and you could easily spend a few hours exploring the halls and shrines. Within the temple complex is the Pagoda of Ten Thousand Buddhas, or Ban Po Thar, which is part of a separate paid area. The pagoda, completed in 1930, is styled with Khmer, Thai and…
spots.price: Free, Entry to Pagoda of Ten Thousand Buddhas: RM6, Funicular train charge: RM6
spots.addr: 1 Tokong Kek Lok Si, off Jl Balik Pulau

spots.name: Penang Hill Mosque
spots.desc: A simple but ornate mosque located at the top of Penang Hill.

spots.name: Sri Aruloli Thirumurugan Temple
spots.desc: A small Hindu temple that is also one of the oldest in Penang.

spots.name: War Memorial Park
spots.desc: A small park that is dedicated to the fallen of World War II.
spots.addr: Cnr Jl Bukit Bendera & Jl Paya Terubong

spots.name: Penang Hill
spots.desc: A hill station established by the British, arguably the best views of George Town and the Malacca Strait can be found here, especially at night. Most people take the funicular rail to the top of the hill. The trains, upgraded in 2011, lift you out of the heat and humidity of the coastal plain and up to a fabulous view and cool breezes, taking around 10min to the top. Those who are adventurous and…
spots.hours: Ticket counter hours: Mon-Fri 06:30-21:00, Sat Sun 06:30-22:00 (Last train to base 1h after counter closes)
spots.price: Funicular fare Malaysians/Foreigners: Adult RM12/30, Child RM6/15 (Fast lane tickets available for about double the…

spots.name: Air Itam Market
spots.desc: The main market within Air Itam, selling almost fresh produce, clothing and other products. The market spills out beyond the main market building and runs along Jl Air Itam. There are also a variety of hawker stalls scattered throughout.
spots.addr: Cnr Jl Pasar and Jl Air Itam

spots.name: Astaka Bukit Bendera
spots.desc: A modern multi-storey hawker centre located at the top of Penang Hill. The hawkers sell some decent local cuisine that you typically see around Penang, with a slight inflation on the price.
spots.addr: Penang Hill Complex, Jl Stesen Bukit Bendera

spots.name: David Brown's Restaurant & Tea Terrace
spots.desc: Set in a British colonial building at the peak of Penang Hill, with colonial decor to match. They serve up Western food including steaks, hearty stews and roasts. For a snack they also sell cakes, scones and sandwiches, along with tea and coffee. There is a nice garden area at the restaurant and the views of the city area are some of the best on Penang Hill.

spots.name: Pasar Air Itam Laksa
spots.desc: A simple and popular hawker at the local market selling one item, Assam Laksa. This particular stall was popularised by a visit from Anthony Bourdain. If you like your food a little spicy be sure to request chilli. Look out for their red sign with gold writing along the outside wall of the market.

spots.name: Sister's Curry Mee
spots.desc: A hawker stall that is popular among locals and run by two elderly sisters, selling Curry Mee.

spots.name: Entopia
spots.desc: More than just a tourist attraction, it is set up as a 'live museum' to educate the public as well as a research centre to develop breeding methods. It houses about 4000 Malaysian butterflies of 120 different species, including the most famous in Malaysia, the Rajah Brooke's Bird wing of the Papilionidae family. Besides, it also exhibits dead-leaf mantis, orchid mantis and Trogonoptera. It also…
spots.price: Admission: adult RM 49 and children RM 29

spots.name: Tropical Spice Garden
spots.desc: The well-done eco-tourism site was set up in 2003 on an old 8-acre rubber plantation, with three trails meandering through the beautiful jungle landscape. Around 500 species of spices, herbs and exotic flora to explore. At one corner is Tree Monkey Cafe (predominantly Thai food) set on a deck in the middle of a rainforest and sea views, and a gift shop and cooking school - these are accessible…
spots.price: Audio tours RM 26, live guided tours RM 35

spots.name: Muka Head Lighthouse
spots.desc: This impressive lighthouse serves as a beacon to sailors and ships in the region. The tower, while not as accessible as other structures on the island, offers spectacular ocean views. There are 2 ways to reach the site: taking boat from Teluk Bahang jetty or climb over the hills by foot.
spots.addr: at the northwestern cape of the Penang island

spots.name: Teluk Bahang Forest Eco Park
spots.desc: A huge recreational forest with about a dozen of marked trails leading to other parts of the island, including Batu Ferringhi proper and Penang Hill, as well as nearby hills and small waterfalls. Part of the park near the entrance is equipped with parking lot, toilets, picnicking and camping facilities, ponds, children playground. Though it's a bit rundown and some maintenance won't harm. There…

spots.name: Penang International Dragon Boat Festival
spots.desc: Staged annually since 1979 and has successfully attracted teams from all over the world including Australia, China, Hong Kong, Japan, Indonesia, the Netherlands, the Philippines, South Africa, Thailand, Canada, and the USA. The event is now usually held at the Teluk Bahang Dam in late May.

spots.name: Batu Ferringhi Night Market
spots.desc: A nightly market that runs the length of the main road through Batu Ferringhi. Set-up along the side walk, this market sells all the typical nick nacks you would expect including DVDs, Jewellery, artworks, crafts, clothing and everything in between. Be prepared to haggle hard as prices are typically inflated due to the markets location along this tourist strip.

spots.name: Tanjung Bungah Market
spots.desc: In the morning a local wet market comes to life selling local fruits, vegetables and other produce. Food is also on the agenda, with many stalls selling food for breakfast. Every Tuesday evening the market opens as a local Pasar Malam, with even more food to entice your taste buds. There are also stalls selling all the typical goods and wares at this market.

spots.name: Lotus Supermarket
spots.desc: Big supermarket with a few other shops and small food court.

spots.name: Fisheries Research Institute Aquarium
spots.desc: A medium-sized aquarium that showcases mostly fish found in regional waters. Nothing fancy but quite informative and enjoyable.
spots.price: Adult RM7, Child (7-12) RM2, Under 7 Free

spots.name: Penang Bridge
spots.desc: With a span of 8.4km over water, it is one of the longest bridges in Asia. The bridge connects the island to the mainland (Seberang Perai) and offers great views of the port and city. You are not supposed to stop on the bridge but many people use the emergency stop areas for a quick photo shoot. The bridge opened to public in 1985 and still is a major national landmark for Malaysia. The , an even…

spots.name: Pulau Jerejak
spots.desc: Also known as the Alcatraz of Malaysia, because the island was once the location of the Jerejak Prison. This beautiful 362 hectare tropical island, is located directly across the channel from Bayan Lepas. The island is now open to the public as a recreational resort. Numerous outdoor activities including nature & historical trekking, mountain biking, and archery are available; personal care such…

spots.name: Snake Temple
spots.desc: Built in 1850 in memory of the renowned Chinese monk Chor Soo Kong. The Snake Temple is on the edge of a highway and is famous for the fact that it has pit vipers living within the temple grounds. Legend has it that Chor Soo Kong, who was also a healer, gave shelter to the snakes of jungle. After the completion of the temple, snakes appeared on their own accord. Today, the snake population of the…

spots.name: War Museum
spots.desc: Located at southeastern tip of Penang, it's a large abandoned military fortress built in the 1930s by the British to protect the southern approaches to the island. The British Royal Engineers and a work force of local labourers blasted and dug into the hill to create a fort with underground military tunnels, an intelligence and logistic centre, halls, offices, ventilation shafts, artillery firing…

spots.name: Penang Golf Club
spots.desc: Renovated in 2012, this Golf club is home to an 18 hole course and driving range. The club also has other facilities including a Japanese restaurant, squash courts, gym, tennis court and snooker rooms.

spots.name: Bukit Jambul Complex
spots.desc: A shopping complex with 414 shops, a Mydin-hypermarket, food court, an amusement center that contain a 40-lane bowling alley and 6 cinema complexes. Lots of shops in the complex have been closed down, but you still get some cheap goods.

spots.name: Queensbay Mall
spots.desc: Bayan Baru. Opened in December 2006, Queensbay Mall is the island's largest mall. It is located next to the sea opposite Pulau Jerejak and is about 20 min drive from the centre of Georgetown. Five levels of retail and 8 levels of parking, Jusco as its anchor tenant, 17 junior anchors, a cineplex, many restaurants and more than 500 retail merchants, including a Borders bookstore.

spots.name: Auto City
spots.desc: Area full of restaurants, pubs and cafes. A lot of youngsters hang out there after 9 or 10PM. Among the shops there are the fast food restaurants KFC, McDonald's, and Subway; the coffee shops Starbucks, Coffee Bean, and Segafredo; the SOHO and Bed pubs; Sushi King, The Manhattan Fish Market, Isshin Japanese Restaurant, Tao Japanese Buffet, Chicago Rib House; and Swensen and Haagen-Dazs for ice…
spots.addr: 1688-F8, Jalan Perusahaan, Highway Auto-City, North-South Highway Juru Interchange

spots.name: Amazing Nibong Tebal
spots.desc: The specific species of mangrove tree which attracts these fireflies is the berembang (sonneratia caseolaris). Firefly watching at Sungai Kerian is increasingly drawing visitors, and the firefly is an icon of Nibong Tebal. The fireflies emit light at the lower abdomen not only to attract mates but also to scare away predators. Their abdomens are filled with a chemical called lucibufagens. Sunset…

spots.name: Bukit Jawi Golf Resort
spots.desc: Lot 414, Mlk6 Jl Paya Kemian Sempayi, Sungai Jawi, Seberang Prai Selatan.

spots.name: Everyday Foodcourt
spots.desc: This foodcourt has almost all the food famous in Malaysia, but located right there all in one place. Try the jumbo size fruit juice.

spots.name: Setia Ecohill Park
spots.desc: A recreational park famous for jogging and exercise. It has many exercise stations and the trail is suitable for cycling.

spots.desc: Groceries, paying tax, drinks, eats, apparels, hardwares, saloon, ATMs.

spots.name: Restoran Itik Salai Mastar
spots.desc: It's in a traditional Malay settlement, down a narrow rural road. Locals come for the smoked duck and beef cooked with hot chilli coconut mixtures. It can be very busy.

spots.name: Lee
spots.desc: Beaufort noodle is the best in town and famous among locals

spots.desc: A temple in Paya Besar.

spots.name: Tesco Kulim
spots.desc: Supermarket.

spots.desc: Malaysian superstore with local and imported products.

spots.desc: superstore and department store.
