spots.desc: grocery and general merchandise.

spots.name: Marco Polo
spots.desc: Good Malaysian and international food and air conditioning.

spots.name: Hard Rock Cafe
spots.desc: Western food, including good burgers. Air conditioned.

spots.name: Bukit Keteri
spots.desc: Limestone hill on the road to Padang Besar.

spots.name: Kota Kayang Museum
spots.desc: An archaeological and Perlis royal family gallery.

spots.name: KFC
spots.desc: Has dodgy Wi-Fi access

spots.name: Gua Kelam
spots.desc: Limestone cave with an old tin mine

spots.name: IOI Mall
spots.desc: Shopping centre with Jusco

spots.name: Carrefour
spots.desc: hypermarket

spots.name: Restaurant 52
spots.desc: Chinese restaurant known for its fresh fish from the river.
spots.addr: Jalan Sungai Lalang Kampung Baru Semenyih

spots.name: Starbucks
spots.desc: There is a Drive-Thru service.

spots.name: Yin Fong Temple
spots.desc: Chinese temple surrounded by Chinese gardens filled with fish ponds, mini zoo, mini gallery and flower gardens.

spots.name: Achya Fruits
spots.desc: Shop selling fresh fruits, especially durians during its season.

spots.name: Dayangs' Camp and Forest Resort
spots.desc: A resort and camp with natural recreational activity facilities.

spots.name: Sinar Eco Resort
spots.desc: Resort with animal encounter, archery, ATV, buggy, cow milking, eco rafting, horse riding, kayaking, KTV, poo and river cruise.
spots.addr: Lot 2346, GM2535, Kampung Sungai Molek, Jeram Batu

spots.name: Poring hot springs
spots.desc: Bathe in the Japanese-style baths. The thermal pools are available as open air style tiled baths with taps to fill with fresh water. For those who are modest or are wanting privacy, enclosed baths inside little chalet-like shelters are available (RM 15 per hour). There is also a small water pool/slide which is used by locals as a bathing area, it is closed on Mondays for cleaning after the…

spots.name: Poring Canopy Walk
spots.desc: Experience a bird's eye view of the surrounding rainforest from about 30 metres above the ground (entrance fee & camera fee, RM5 for a mobile phone camera). The walking path from the ticket booth to the beginning of the canopy walk is about 500m up hill and is moderately aerobic. It is a circular route.This pathway is not suitable for those who have mobility restrictions. If you are afraid of…

spots.name: Little India
spots.desc: Beautifully restored street with all types of Indian shops and restaurants.

spots.name: Cycle or hike on SWBC
spots.desc: If you need a break from the city hustle and bustle then try this: Walk or cycle on the Mid Valley-Dataran Merdeka Bike Lane, which was inaugurated in 2015. You can venture either towards the Mid Valley shopping mall (the largest in KL) or to Merdeka Square.

spots.name: Bangsar Village II
spots.desc: This is another favourite with those staying around Bangsar & Damansara Heights neighbourhood. Bangsar Village 2 is linked to the original Bangsar Village by a covered pedestrian bridge.

spots.name: Bangsar Shopping Centre
spots.desc: Better known as BSC, this mini shopping centre is a favourite among expats and the locals staying around the Bangsar & Damansara Heights neighbourhood. Plenty of cafes & restaurants - a good spot to meet up with friends. BSC also features speciality stores plus Jasons Supermarket.

spots.name: Peter's Pork Noodle
spots.desc: This food stall in the well hidden Money's corner food court is considered one of the best pork noodle places in whole Kuala Lumpur. You can choose between a big (RM 9.50) or small (RM 8.50) bowl, 3 different types of noodles and with or without (-RM 0.50) an egg on top. Try to avoid the peak hours (weekdays from 11:30 to 13:30). During those times it is hard to find a table due to large groups…

spots.name: Devi's Corner
spots.desc: Great banana leaf restaurant. It is not as famous as the nearby Nirwana banana leaf restaurant, but cheaper and - according to many locals - has better tasting food.

spots.name: Alexis Bistro & Wine Bar
spots.desc: Restaurant, which houses live performances - mainly jazz - on almost every weekend. Local and international artists are performing.

spots.name: Petrosains
spots.desc: An exhibit of the science and technology behind the petroleum industry, mainly aimed for children and sponsored by the Petronas oil company. There are various science shows, interactive exhibits and simulation experiences throughout. Book tickets at least 30 minutes in advance, or even a few days earlier if you can. Can be very busy on weekends.
spots.price: Foreigners/Malaysians: adults RM25/15, children RM15/5, seniors RM18/8, family (2 adults & 2 children) RM50/30

spots.name: Berjaya Times Square Theme Park
spots.desc: Malaysia's largest indoor theme park, located on the upper floors of the giant Berjaya Times Square mall and particularly notable for its hair-raising seven-story indoor roller coaster. The park is divided into two sections, one geared for small children, the other for those who want a little more excitement; one ticket gets you into both.
spots.price: Foreigners/Malaysians: adults RM48/38, children RM38/28, family (2 adults & 2 children) RM138/106

spots.name: Dharma Realm Monastery Canteen
spots.desc: Great vegetarian food prepared by volunteers. Earnings are used to maintain the temple. A favourite among local office workers. The food is free of charge on Fridays and Sundays. Feel free to leave a donation though.

spots.name: Horizon Grill
spots.desc: Great fusion food with stunning views towards the Petronas Towers.

spots.name: Luna Bar
spots.desc: Menara PanGlobal 34F, Jalan Punchak (off Jl P. Ramlee). - Super-chic breezy rooftop bar with a pool in the middle and the best night views in town. Show up early to grab a romantic windowside niche. Drinks RM20 and up, cover charge of RM50 (incl. one drink) may apply on weekends after 21:30.

spots.name: Sky Bar
spots.desc: Incredible bar with great views over the city and the Twin Towers.Located on the top floor of the Traders Hotel, it is built around the Hotel swimming pool. Loud techno music late at night. Best place to be around sunset. be prepared to pay 5 star hotel prices. One of the best places in town before dinner.

spots.name: Heli Lounge
spots.desc: Amazing location on a helipad high above the city with amazing views.

spots.name: Art Deco architecture
spots.desc: This stretch of Jalan Tuanku Abdul Rahman, starting from Sogo and Odeon Cinema in the north, and ending at Euro Moda in the south, contains a very large collection of Kuala Lumpur's art deco colonial buildings. Check out for the pink Euro Moda building, the pink-and-yellow Aidijuma store, the green Gulati's store and the Odeon Cinema. Sadly there were reports that Odeon Cinema will be demolished…

spots.name: Bazaar Baru Chow Kit
spots.desc: Boasting the title as the largest wet market in Kuala Lumpur this market gives a glimpse of how ordinary Malaysians do their daily shopping. In addition to fresh fruit, vegetables, meat and seafood you will also find stalls selling silks, fabrics, shoes and other nicknacks without the tourist price inflation. Food stalls are scattered throughout the markets too.

spots.name: Taman Budaya Kuala Lumpur
spots.desc: It is used as a theatre and arts centre. This building is notable for being the first site of the Victoria Institution until 1929 (refer below). In 1911 it was witness to a sensational murder case - the Ethel Proudlock case. The building was once part of a larger school complex; the other buildings were torn down in the 1960s. Gutted in a fire in 1999, it was refurbished after acquisition by the…

spots.name: Medan Pasar (Market Square) Clock Tower
spots.desc: Art-Deco clock tower built in 1936/37 to commemorate the coronation of King George VI. The commemorative plague was removed upon Malayan independence in 1957. Refurbished in 2013. The Market Square is no longer open to vehicular traffic since then. There is a fountain on the southern side of the clock tower.

spots.name: Oriental Building
spots.desc: Stately Art Deco building towering above the Masjid Jamek metro station. Completed 1933, it was reportedly Kuala Lumpur's tallest structure back then. During the post-war years it was home to Radio Malaya (now Radio Television Malaysia, RTM). In the 1990s and early 2000s it housed a bank, which has since relocated. The building is vacant, though occasionally its five-foot ways are illuminated at…

spots.name: Guan Di Temple
spots.desc: Located across the road from the Sri Mahariamman Temple, this is one of two 19th-century Chinese temples in the district. Built in 1888, this temple is dedicated to the Han Dynasty/Three Kingdoms figure Guan Yu (aka Kwan Kung). Though not as well-known as the Sin Sze Si Ya Temple, it is still very popular. This temple is also the office of the Selangor and Kuala Lumpur Kwong Siew Association.

spots.name: Swimming classes at the National Aquatic Center
spots.desc: Olympic size pool. The opening hours are a little weird though: 7 one-hourly sessions on weekdays and 3 evening sessions on the weekends.
spots.price: Adults: RM6; senior citizens and the disabled: RM5

spots.name: Publika
spots.desc: Great place with plenty of hip stores. Plenty of food choices and a great supermarket in the basement.

spots.name: AEON Ayer Keroh
spots.desc: The second oldest AEON shopping in Malaysia, you can buy almost all things here from clothing, electronics or retail shopping. They also provide variety of Japanese food and snack if you craving for Japanese food. Although the name is AEON Ayer Keroh, it is actually located at Bukit Baru, which situated around 10 kilometres from Ayer Keroh PLUS Toll Plaza.

spots.name: Ayer Keroh Food Court
spots.desc: There are tons of local food sell here like Nasi Lemak, Satay, Curry Noodle and the favourite of Asam Pedas. If you plan to go there by car, there are many parking spots (around 20) in front of the food court. If you plan to go there by public bus, you need to stop at bus stop nearer to traffic light intersection of Ayer Keroh Industrial Park, from there, the walking distance to the food court is…

spots.name: Jelewang Waterfall and Stong Hill Resort
spots.desc: The Jelewang Waterfall is one of the tallest in South East Asia and is visible all the way from Dabong.You can go to Stong Hill Resort (10RM entry) and head up the hill to the suspension bridge to get a decent view of the waterfall.The 10RM entry fee covers all of the pools and cascades below the suspension bridge and it is well worth throwing on your aqua shoes and traversing down the hill…

spots.name: Gua Ikan Cave Complex
spots.desc: There is a system of five caves, all located near Gua Ikan (fish cave). It is only 3-4 km outside town. It is very interesting to see the mountains and stone formations, and there are turtles, birds, bats, crabs and more in the cave. If you go, bring good shoes (it is not recommended to wade in the waters), and mosquito repellent (lots of mosquitos). Gua Ikan is free to enter and lit up by…

spots.name: Hike Guning Stong
spots.desc: It is possible to hike to the top of Jelewang waterfall and to Gunung Stong but you need a guide for both. The guide is priced for groups of people (I was quoted 300) so make sure you have some friends to bring with you. You can do a day trip to the top of the waterfall or multi day hikes to the hills within the park.

spots.name: kedai makan kak ros
spots.desc: Yummy, cheap and easy with a menu that has a good spread of options

spots.name: Pasar Malam
spots.desc: There's a night market on Saturday night with a variety of cooked, fresh and deep fried food along with clothes and other random stalls.

spots.name: Clock Tower
spots.desc: The clocktower looms over the town, gives you a fairly impressive view of the surrounding hills and is a perfect viewpoint to climb up, especially during the night when the town lights are lit. There is an elevator.

spots.name: Colmar Tropicale
spots.desc: This small French village modeled after a place of the same name in France is rather picturesque (which will excite photo enthusiasts) and makes for a great place for relaxing. It is suitable as a romantic getaway for couples or a family escape for families. The crowd would swell on weekends as city-goers would usually come here for a close retreat away from the rush and bustle of the city.

spots.name: Game Room
spots.desc: Most likely built with children in mind, the game room has pool tables, foosball tables, and board games to entertain and spend free time.

spots.name: The beach
spots.desc: The main attraction here is the wide sandy beach. Water activities including yachting, surfing, kitesurfing, windsurfing, swimming, etc are available from guesthouses. As of July 2017, you had to share the water with naughty stingy jellyfishes.

spots.name: Cherating Turtle Sanctuary
spots.desc: Centre dedicated to the protection of turtles. It focuses on improving the survival rate of hatchlings on the nearby beach. Cherating is the only place in Malaysia where leatherback turtles lay their eggs hence the importance of theirs activities. The centre is not of great interest for visitors and provide only few information on the local sea fauna. Few rescued turtles and hatchlings can be…
spots.hours: Tue-Sun 9AM-1PM, 2-5PM; on Fri the centre is closed from noon-3PM for prayer

spots.name: Cherating Point
spots.desc: Well established school in town. The school is located at Matahari Holiday huts and offers packages for multiple lessons with accommodation. Board hire starts at 45RM for 1/2 day. Package starts at 470RM for 2 days and 2 lessons with accommodation.
spots.hours: Opens from November to March only

spots.name: Kam's surf shack
spots.desc: Specialized in water sports rental: surf, windsurf, kite surf and even x-sailing. You can also get food and drinks there.

spots.name: Batik painting
spots.desc: Classes are offered by some handicraft shops on the main street.

spots.name: Nabil's Cafe
spots.desc: Good spot for local or western dinner. Can be closed during off season.

spots.name: Ombok Cafe
spots.desc: Cafe, restaurant, art gallery, and surfing shop. The place was opened as a surf shop to provide surf and environment awareness. Great laid back vibes and super friendly owner. Simple food but probably the best in town.

spots.name: Warong Ambak
spots.desc: Popular with locals for breakfast. Cheap roti canai and tea tarik

spots.name: Pulau Santap
spots.desc: What happens when two rivers meet? A kind of chemistry takes place. The meeting of the Bunus and Ceringging rivers is the birthplace of Janda Baik. In the early days, there was a small islet where Sultan Abu Bakar of Pahang took his meals. Santap is the language of the royal courts which means the Sultan is having his meal. The place was aptly named Pulau Santap. The islet is no more to be seen…

spots.name: Ulu Tampit Waterfall
spots.desc: Ulu Tampit waterfall is in Latto Charok. It is recommended to visit the waterfall if you are visiting Janda Baik. Many would find that Ulu Tampit waterfall is the most enjoyable one! There are seven floors of waterfall and 4th, 5th and 7th floor, are the most common floors people go to visit. It only takes about 45 minutes of light trekking and hiking through the jungle to get to the top floor.…

spots.name: Mount Nuang
spots.desc: Gunung Nuang or Mount Nuang (1493m) is the highest in the state of Selangor, which is in Hulu Langat. Gunung Nuang is among the famous mountain for local and foreign trekkers and it is also a "training centre" for those who plan to challenge the Mount Tahan in Pahang and Mount Kinabalu in Sabah. Trekking up Gunung Nuang in Hulu Langat offers intrepid trekkers endless opportunities to observe…

spots.name: Orang Asli Museum
spots.desc: The Orang Asli Museum in Jalan Gombak, 24 km away from Janda Baik and Batu Caves, is an impressive and informative centre showcasing the history, customs and traditions as well as the social and economic development of the peninsula's early inhabitants.; Managed by the Orang Asli Affairs Department, the museum displays models and exhibits highlighting the lifestyle of the tribes including their…

spots.name: Di Hilir Brasserie
spots.desc: This elegant restaurant is located at the Seri Pengantin Resort in Kampung Sum-Sum Hilir Off Kampung Janda Baik. Embark on a culinary adventure, a dwelling within lush tropical environs within scenic view of the resort's swimming pool and the Sum-Sum Hilir River. The menu commands as much as the views, ranging from local favorites, Western classics to Asian exotics.

spots.name: Restaurant Budiyah
spots.desc: Located at the stretch of shoplots at the downhill of Kampung Bukit Tinggi and nearby to a BP petrol station. Also, this restaurant can be easily seen and accessed from the main highway. This restaurant is popular among the highway stopovers and the locals as they serving fresh hot 'kelantanese' dishes and pahang's specialities.Operates from morning till late daily.

spots.name: Restaurant Cik Mek
spots.desc: Located in Kg. Cheringging off Kampung Janda Baik. Served hot from the kitchen. This restaurant is popular for its Kelantanese food and live cable television entertainment showing the latest sports.

spots.name: Genting Sempah Rest Area
spots.desc: There are endless choice of eateries in this area. One of the popular ones is McDonald Restaurant which also have a 24-hour drive-thru counter.

spots.name: Restaurant Foon Lock, Kg. Bukit Tinggi
spots.desc: Popular among the highway stopovers and the locals. Serving lip-smacking Chinese dishes and great friendly service too!

spots.name: Minang Sri Selera
spots.desc: It is the best minang restaurant in Janda Baik. Its located in the Kg Sum Sum. The special menu is the Sup Tulang and Cendul Pulut.
spots.addr: Warung Minang Sri Selera, Kg Sum-Sum

spots.name: Tenggol Coral Beach Resort
spots.desc: This PADI dive centre does everything including dive packages, NITROX and dive training courses.

spots.name: Koref Desaru Leisure Farm
spots.desc: An eco resort with outdoor water challenge, tree house & vegetable garden.

spots.name: Pengerang British coastal battery
spots.desc: site of a major World War II-era British coastal battery. The part of it at Pengelih, right next to the immigration point, is open to the public but in a state of nature, with no trails, signs, etc. Most of the rest is now used by the Malaysian military.

spots.name: Rumah Rakit Ikhwan
spots.desc: Leisure center for river-related water activities as well as accommodation.
spots.addr: PTD 60, Kampung Air Bentan, Ladang Sungai Papan, Bandar Penawar 81900

spots.name: Jade Garden Seafood Corner
spots.desc: The largest and most famous operation in town, now in a large, airy air-conditioned hall at the seafront. Laden with tanks of doomed crustaceans and even a hotel. Prices are clearly marked and the extensive menu has plenty of other options as well, including a number of fish grown/kept in nets out back. Try the Lobster in Superior Broth or the somewhat sweet deep-fried Cereal Lobster.
spots.addr: Lot 4785, No. 1, Jalan Siakap, Kampung Sungai Rengit

spots.name: Butterfly Park
spots.desc: A short walk within the park en route to the canopy walk (entrance fee). Note this closes at 4pm, earlier than the rest of the park.

spots.name: Rafflesia keithii
spots.desc: The world's largest flower known to reach almost a metre in diameter. Its bud takes a full year to grow until it finally blossoms, but then withers after only one week in bloom. The interior of the blossom smells like rotten meat, attracting flying insects that then pollinate it.
spots.price: RM30 additional to hot springs entrance fee

spots.name: Trekking
spots.desc: For those keen to explore, trek through the lowland forest 13 km to the waterfall. The nearer pool is 8 km. You do not need a guide for either trek.

spots.name: Langanan Waterfall
spots.desc: Larger and more impressive than Kipungit waterfall. 1.5h hike away from Poring. The trek closes at 14:00.

spots.name: Matang Wildlife Centre
spots.desc: It is part of Kubah National Park and is popular with families who picnic by the refreshing rock pools and waterfalls. There are full facilities including toilets and BBQs. There are four relatively easy jungle trails, but the main attraction used to be the Orang Utan Training Centre - where orphaned and rescued orangutans are rehabilitated and taught how to survive in the wild. But after a…

spots.name: ATM
spots.desc: The town has a Bank Simpanan National, with ATM. In case your card is quite sensitive, is better to withdraw money in previous cities before you run out.

spots.name: Sarawak Cultural Village
spots.desc: This living museum depicts the heritage of the major racial groups in Sarawak. Here, it is possible to see Sarawak's ethnic diversity at a glance. The handicraft is both bewildering and tempting. You can also try hands-on with making of these handicrafts. The 45-minute cultural performance of songs, dances and entertainment is something you will not want to miss out during your visit to Sarawak.…

spots.name: Rainforest World Music Festival
spots.desc: Internationally famous festival bringing together musicians from a variety the many tribes of Borneo

spots.name: Damai Beach
spots.desc: Kuching's nearest public beach. There is a small section of beach which is free to use by the public and has nice sand with hermit crabs who rush about and burrow under the sand when you approach them! The water is very warm but not particularly clear but gently sloping for safe swimming. Beware of rocks at high tide, though. Parasols and kayaks can be hired. Busy at weekends.

spots.name: Sarawak Jungle Trek
spots.desc: Short marked circular trail through relatively level jungle terrain

spots.name: Simunjan Coal Mines, Ruins
spots.desc: The Simunjan Coal Works area, Gunung Ngeli, an historic mining hill exploited by first the British and then the Japanese. With a bit of trekking several interesting mine entrances can be viewed in a fun day outing from Simunjan town. The jungle and farms of the foothills make for an attraction on their own right, the mines scattered more or less close to the overgrown remains of an old coal road…

spots.name: Simujan river boat ramp
spots.desc: Here on the Simujan river, a branch or the Sadong, various small long boats leave every hour or so to villages close by. Ask the other waiting passengers where they are going and when a boat returns. Barges can be seen off loading timber and gravel.

spots.name: PPIK community Internet
spots.desc: Free public Internet with 4 computers. Open in the daytime only, though if the only staff member is otherwise occupied it might be closed. If so there is an Internet gaming shop in the backstreet behind the hotel, but this might be quite noisy.

spots.name: Play Futsul
spots.desc: With the friendly local kids, after school, or morning and afternoon on the Weekend.

spots.name: 15 Yap Siew Seng
spots.desc: Serves good home cooking style Chinese food, and is one of the few non-noodle places open at night.

spots.name: Chop Simunjan Cafe
spots.desc: Serves one of the best breakfast Laksas, with a generous serving of Udang

spots.name: Bambo_cafe and catering Kpg Nanas
spots.desc: Serves good home cooking, village food, alacarte, Ayam Penyet, laksa sarawak and many more. 7PM-midnight.
spots.addr: Kpg Nanas main road to simunjan bazar

spots.name: Jaya Restoran
spots.desc: Great selection of Indian dishes. Very fresh ingredients. Especially the lunch buffet is highly recommended.
spots.price: RM8-14 for an average lunch w/o drinks

spots.name: Annalakshmi Vegetarian Restaurant
spots.desc: Famous vegetarian restaurant at the Temple of Fine Arts, with occasional cultural shows. Food is no longer priced based on a pay-as-you-wish model; the restaurant charges set prices for food. Menu consists of buffet lunch, rotis for breakfast/tea and ala carte for dinner. Dress code: No shorts/slippers.
spots.price: From RM 10 for lunch or dinner

spots.name: Chat Masala
spots.desc: This vegetarian restaurant serves mock meat. Go for the "mutton" or "chicken" briyani, tea-time specials like pani puri or bhel puri, then wash it down with filter coffee.

spots.name: Kaveri
spots.desc: Open fronted restaurant with friendly staff. Serves a variety of Indian foods, plenty of meat dishes, as well as a number of vegetarian options.
spots.price: RM1 for roti canai, RM4-5 for meat

spots.name: Saravanaa Bhavan
spots.desc: Clean restaurant serving authentic South Indian cuisine. All food is vegetarian.
spots.price: RM13 for set meal of rice, papadum, chapati and a selection of 10 chutneys and dhals

spots.name: Vishalatchi Food Catering
spots.desc: Specialises in authentic Chettinad cuisine served on banana leaf. Try the idli or puri for breakfast.

spots.name: Chynna
spots.desc: Wonderfully over-the-top modern Chinese restaurant that looks like it just stepped out of a kung-fu movie, with waitresses in thigh-slit cheongsams and plaited houseboys serving herbal tea from a pot with a meter-long spout. The menu is equally eclectic: try the pumpkin and shrimp dumplings or the chicken feet in black bean sauce, then finish off with coconut ice cream in avocado sauce. Lunchtime…

spots.name: Sage
spots.desc: Chef Daniel has now exceeded his master Takashi Kimura and taken Sage to new heights. With a combination of Japanese and Italian flavours, he bring fusion food to a new level of delicateness without compromise. Sage has been attracting hordes of customers from his previous restaurant Cilantro's which is closed for renovation. One of the best restaurants in Kuala Lumpur but expect to spend about…
spots.addr: Level 6, The Gardens Residences, Mid Valley City

spots.name: The Social
spots.desc: Popular bar and restaurant.Can get quite noisy due to the large crowd.

spots.name: Great Eastern Mall
spots.desc: Great Eastern Mall is adjoined with the Menara Great Eastern and professes to offer a 'fine lifestyle and relaxation' shopping experience.

spots.name: Rama V
spots.desc: Among the best Thai food in town. Main dishes are around RM60.

spots.name: Zouk
spots.desc: A branch of the famous Singaporean club, opened in 2004. Plays dance/house style music on Friday nights and popular with younger clubbers and rich locals (Ferrari parked outside for show). Dress well and in black. RM40 entry for men, RM30 for women (incl. one drink), and from RM25 per drink. Popular on Wednesday nights for Mambo where they play popular music from the 1070s and 80s.

spots.name: Craft Village @ Kompleks Kraf KL
spots.desc: Part of a government-owned organisation which was set up to showcase Malaysian art and craft. You can create your own Malay art by having a dabble at batik drawing, wood carving and pottery making, all at a 'minimal fee'. While there you can also explore the museum, gift shop and café.

spots.name: Diving @ Aquaria KLCC
spots.desc: Take a plunge (literally) and explore Aquaria KLCC with the resident aquatic animals. The Cage Rage package takes you underwater in the safety of a cage. Be sure to say hello to the sharks when down there. The Dive with Sharks package is definitely for who are more adventurous, where you can explore the underwater area without a cage and get up close to the aquatic life. You also get a…
spots.price: Cage Rage: RM199, Dive With Sharks: RM400 (Requires diving card and log book)
spots.addr: Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre Complex, Jl Pinang

spots.name: Pamper Zone
spots.desc: An impressive cluster of spas within Starhill Gallery, with services ranging from world class all day treatments (RM600), to affordable facials and one hour long full body massages (RM100).

spots.name: Lot 10 Hutong
spots.desc: This shopping mall in the Golden Triangle has a collection of 20 street vendors who were invited to relocate in the food court. Provides an excellent spread of Malaysian food in hygienic and air-conditioned food court comfort at prices that are only slightly above those outdoors. Many famous Chinese style and KL-based foods are served in this food court.
spots.addr: Cnr Jl Bukit Bintang & Jl Sultan Ismail

spots.name: Bijan
spots.desc: 3 Jln Ceylon - Modern-styled décor in a home-like setting with outdoor verandah-garden compliments the well prepared (though perhaps slightly overpriced) Malaysian food. Classy patrons and impeccable service however make it worth a try.

spots.name: Glutton Street Market
spots.desc: Another street full of food stalls similar to Jalan Alor, but a lot less touristy and more authentic.

spots.name: Super Noodle House
spots.desc: One of the best Hong Kong-style restaurants in KL. Menu includes porridge, wantan mee or chicken rice. Good food with reasonable pricing.
spots.addr: LG-001, Lower Ground, Sungai Wang Shopping Centre, Jalan Sultan Ismail

spots.name: Overseas restaurant
spots.desc: A popular Chinese restaurant attracting a clientele ranging from local billionaires to middle class families. Food is outstanding and if you care to take a little time and book a day or two earlier you can order any number of special dishes that are typically but not necessarily more expensive. Service is haphazard and as prices are cheap, a discrete tip to one of the Captains and the waitress…

spots.name: Passage Thru' India
spots.desc: An excellent Indian restaurant that offers both northern and southern Indian cuisine. Favorites here include the Chicken Beriyani, Chicken Tandoori, Chukka Mutton, Fried Fish, Malabar Avial and the slightly expensive but very tasty PTI Prawn masala.
spots.addr: 4 Jl Delima (several other locations through Malaysia)

spots.name: Restoran Ganesh
spots.desc: A fantastic place, Indian food that you don't get at most places, served on banana leaves.

spots.name: Uncle Jack Fried Chicken
spots.desc: set 1. one piece of chicken with chicken rice and a drink . Ice cream cone is just 0.50c
spots.price: a meal with drink for RM4.29
spots.addr: Sungei Wang Plaza Jl Bukit Bintang

spots.name: Havana Bar and Grill
spots.desc: Bar and grill in a quaint old building serving pan-Western cuisine and an extensive drinks list, turning into a nightclub later on. Features a pleasant outdoor seating area with a smoking section and Cuban cigars for sale; these aren't cheap due to high local taxes, but you can bring your own for no extra charge.

spots.name: Sahara Tent
spots.desc: Large, authentic and popular Middle Eastern eatery in Ain Arabia, KL's Little Arabia. The giant mezze platter (RM29) will leave two stuffed and a shisha water pipe at RM10 tops off the meal nicely.
spots.addr: 87 Jalan Berangan, off Jalan Bukit Bintang

spots.name: Twenty One Bar and Kitchen
spots.desc: Stylish bar and restaurant. Great contemporary food. The bar is very popular at night. Affordable lunch deals at RM30. Mains RM30-60.

spots.name: EEST @ The Westin Kuala Lumpur
spots.desc: EEST is a prominent Asian restaurant in Kuala Lumpur. Savour the blend of authentic flavours specially selected from Asian cultures right here in Kuala Lumpur. Indulge in Asian flavours at EEST with a selection of Asian cuisine to delight your palate.

spots.name: Bistro de Paris
spots.desc: The French dining experience from aperitif to digestif, ranging from steak frites to crême brulée. Open daily from 11AM until late. Lunch prix fixe at RM15.95, dinner prix fixe at RM69.95.

spots.name: El Cerdo
spots.desc: German-run eatery with kitschy pig-themed decor specializing in all things pork, particularly Spanish treats like jamón serrano and whole suckling pig, complete with ceremonial plate-breaking. Organic lamb ribs are excellent. Portions are generous and quality is excellent. The place is usually packed and noisy, so book ahead (esp. on weekends).

spots.name: Neroteca
spots.desc: Italian restaurant and deli, specialized in pork meat. They serve great Italian hearty food with one of a great selection of Italian cured meats and cheeses, also for take away. Open from 9:3AM (Tuesdays from 3PM) until midnight.

spots.name: Pinchos Tapas Bar
spots.desc: Pinchos is a great place to meet and mingle over a pitcher of their sangria and plates of their delicious tapas. In the evenings, Pinchos is one of the hottest places to be. After midnight, it really kicks off as patrons try to squeeze in to the restaurant-bar that’s already bursting at the seams. Expect to guzzle down one of their Spanish drinks like the Estrella Damm, the beer of Barcelona or…

spots.name: Dark Caves
spots.desc: Just off to the side of the entrance to the Batu Caves is the Dark Caves. The Dark Caves is a conservation site showcasing the endemic animals and insects that live in the cave ecosystem. Times for tours depend on the number of visitors but maximum waiting time is 20 minutes. Beware the monkeys.

spots.name: Kepong Metropolitan Park
spots.desc: Located at the northern side of Kepong 6 km from Sri Hartamas, this place features a lake and is ideal for flying kites. Jogging/cycling tracks, remote control car track, football field and observation tower are among the facilities provided.

spots.name: Vertical Adventure
spots.desc: Day trip outdoor rock climbing at Batu Caves suitable for every fitness, age and gender.

spots.name: Yu Ai Segambut Seafood Noodle
spots.desc: Truly a local's recommendation. Noodles come with three soup options: their famous curry laksa, tom yam or qingtang (clear soup). Air-cond seating upstairs.

spots.name: Masjid India Bazaar
spots.desc: A covered bazaar stretching out from LRT Masjid Jamek, along Jalan Melayu towards Masjid India, quite similar in feel to the more famous Jalan Petaling (with a similar plastic overhang) but not as large or crowded -- not necessarily a bad thing.

spots.name: Pasar Malam
spots.desc: A long night market spanning the entire length of the 'lorong'. This weekly night market is an experience whether you are looking for a bargain, local products, or just an authentic Malaysian market experience. Food stalls are scattered throughout the market and is a great experience outside the typical tourist scene. During the Muslim fasting month of Ramadan it operates daily and expands to the…

spots.name: Campbell Complex
spots.desc: Great shopping centre to buy textiles. Site of the infamous Campbell Complex fire in 1976, regarded as Malaysia's own "Towering Inferno".

spots.name: Plaza City One
spots.desc: Textile and fashion stores congregate here. At the second floor above ground level there is a food court (see 'Eat' section below).

spots.name: Semua House
spots.desc: Fashion, cosmetics, perfume, and jewellery. There is a Burger King store at the ground-level entrance. Food court located one floor below ground.

spots.name: GS Gills
spots.desc: The top sporting goods distributes in Mayalsia, carrying all sorts of sporting equipment and attire.
spots.addr: 9th Floor, Wisma Harwant, 106 Jalan Tuanku Adbul Rahman

spots.name: Pertama Complex
spots.desc: Opened in 1976 as Kuala Lumpur's third shopping mall, and still good for cheap shoes, leather ware and other knick-knacks.

spots.name: Sogo Shopping Complex
spots.desc: Probably the biggest department store you will ever see, with 10 floors of shopping, dining and entertainment. If you budget permits, you can shop here for everything from clothing to high-tech toys.

spots.name: Wisma Shen (Haniffa Department Store)
spots.desc: StarPoints Hotel occupies the upper floors of the building. On the ground level there is a Haniffa Department Store. Do check out Haniffa for its large collection of chocolates.

spots.name: Lulu Hypermarket
spots.desc: Arab-owned LuLu Hypermarket opened its first store in Malaysia here. Hypermarket and fresh produce on the ground level. Ethnic fashion and pharmacy on the first floor, electronics, stationery, furnishing and sporting goods on the second floor. There is a food court on the fourth floor, not accessible from within LuLu Hypermarket, but on an escalator outside the hypermarket's compound.
spots.addr: Lot 159 Persiaran CapSquare Off Jalan Munshi Abdullah

spots.name: Busana Menara Mara
spots.desc: State-owned commercial centre featuring Malay textile, fashion, arts and crafts stores. Level 3 is home to MARA Digital, dedicated to computers and IT equipment. Located just next to Pertama Complex, walking distance from Sogo and Bandaraya metro station.
spots.addr: Menara MARA, Lot C, 232, Jalan Tuanku Abdul Rahman

spots.name: Maju Junction
spots.desc: This vacant shopping mall is a pit stop for pedestrians walking from Jalan Tuanku Abdul Rahman to Quill City Mall and the Sultan Ismail metro station.

spots.name: Mydin Wholesale Emporium
spots.desc: Mydin supermarket chain has an outlet tucked away in this corner of Masjid India/Masjid Jamek district. It is reportedly Mydin's first store in Kuala Lumpur/Klang Valley. It is along the same street with Haniffa.

spots.name: Capital Cafe
spots.desc: Opposite Jalan Tuanku Abdul Rahman from the Sogo mall. Known to be one of the oldest cafes along Jalan Tuanku Abdul Rahman. Founded in the 1940s, popular until now.
spots.addr: 213, Jalan Tuanku Abdul Rahman, City Centre

spots.name: RA Nasi Lemak
spots.desc: Serving up the Malaysian breakfast favourite, Nasi Lemak, and a range of drinks including Teh Tarik. A plate of rice is given to you then you add whatever you like on a self-serve basis. Located just at the western exit of Dang Wangi metro station.

spots.name: Yut Kee Restaurant
spots.desc: A true KL establishment, this Chinese coffeeshop is famous for its Hainanese-style chicken chop and roti babi, pork sandwich. It has relocated to a larger building behind its former site.

spots.name: Plaza City One Food Court
spots.desc: Check out the food court on Level 2 of Plaza City One for its Indian, Pakistani and Bangladeshi cuisine. Recommended: Hanif Mughal Food (stall 5), Nasi Arab (stall 3) and Punjabi Vegetarian Food (stall 8).

spots.name: Kudu bin Abdul Nasi Kandar
spots.desc: Famous Nasi Kandar restaurant near the junction with Jalan Sultan Ismail. The late Malaysian artist P. Ramlee was reportedly a fan - his former film studio was located across the street. Walking distance from Sultan Ismail metro station, opposite Tune Hotel and near Maju Junction.
spots.addr: 335, Jalan Tuanku Abdul Rahman, Medan Tuanku

spots.name: Coliseum Cafe and Bar
spots.desc: A KL legend, this colonial-style hangout hasn't changed its appearance or staff in over 90 years. In the late 2010s, this restaurant has expanded to Mid Valley, Petaling Jaya and Subang Jaya. Service is surly and the tablecloths could use a good wash, but their Western food, particularly the "sizzling" steaks on a hot plate (from RM35), is still one of the best deals in town. Also try a freshly…

spots.name: Second-hand/out-of-season cloths
spots.desc: Near this GPS marker you will find two Muslim-run cloths shops which sell dirt-cheap second-hand and out-of-season cloths, both to the west and east inside the buildings on the ground floor. Fancy a decent white shirt for RM6.50 or some pants for RM15, you will find them here.

spots.name: KK Super Mart
spots.desc: 24 hour convenience store. There is another store at Jalan Sultan.

spots.name: Bunn Choon Restaurant
spots.desc: Old-time Chinese kopitiam, operating since the 19th century, serving noodles, dim sum, as well as pastries. Do check out the dining area on the mezzanine floor - very faithful reproduction of a colonial-era Chinese living room, complete with a woodern stair, artifacts, decor and even electrical switches from that era.
spots.hours: Daily 7:30AM to about 4PM, depending on stocks

spots.name: Kim Lian Kee
spots.desc: Right in the middle of Petaling Street, at the crossroads with Jalan Hang Lekir. In business since the 1920s, this stall was regarded as the inventor of KL-styled hokkien fried mee. No English sign, no menu in any language, and a kitchen you really don't want to look into - but it packs the crowds for its famous hokkien mee (fried noodles in dark sauce, RM5). Wash it down with a RM1 mug of…

spots.name: Soong Kee Beef Noodles
spots.desc: This is a well-known KL beef noodle shop, it is said to have started operating since 1945. It serves the noodles "dry" with beef mince while the beef balls are given separately in a bowl of soup.

spots.name: Sin Kiew Yee Shin Kee Beef Noodles
spots.desc: Also very traditional beef noodles like before, but more choices and also very popular with locals and tourists. 3 different noodles, 3 different ways of beef, dry or wet.

spots.name: Lebuh Ampang banana leaf restaurants
spots.desc: Located adjacent to Masjid Jamek station, the street is lined with Indian banana leaf rice shops, just make your pick. One of them is Lakshmi Villas. For purely vegetarian food, you can try Saravanaa Bhavan or Bakti Woodlands.

spots.name: Central Market Food Court
spots.desc: Food court on Central Market's mezzanine floor, one of the few air-conditioned eating places in the area.

spots.name: Kedai Makanan Daun Pisang Vinny Jeyaa
spots.desc: typical Indian restaurant (as for Malaysia) but with exceptionally wide choice of Indian delicacies (both veg and non-veg). Very friendly staff and budget prices - full meal with drinks for two = around RM13.

spots.name: Ho Kow Hainam Kopitiam
spots.desc: Hainanese kopitiam in business since 1956 serving typical koptiam fare (nasi lemak, chicken hor fun, kaya toast etc). Watch out for the long queues; advisable to come early. Stocks do run out quick, usually by 2 pm.
spots.hours: Daily 7:30AM-3PM, though stocks may run out early

spots.name: Texas Chicken
spots.desc: One of only 2 remaining Western fast-food joints in this area (and the only one to operate 24/7), after a McDonald's at the entrance of Petaling Street ceased operations a few years ago, followed by a former Subway opposite Kotaraya complex. It is on the same side of the road as the Lai Foong kopitiam.
spots.addr: Lot G.02, Ground Floor, Wisma Fui Chiu, No. 32, Jalan Tun Tan Cheng Lock

spots.name: KFC
spots.desc: The other Western fast-food joint in this area (coincidentally, fried chicken as well).

spots.name: San Francisco Coffee Express
spots.desc: Hot and cold coffee beverages and delicious cakes of all kinds.
spots.addr: LG-022 Lower Ground Floor, City Square Mall

spots.name: Reggae Bar
spots.desc: It is a hostel bar so it is popular with backpackers. They also serve Asian and Western food. Also a hostel!

spots.name: Bukit Jalil National Stadium
spots.desc: Bukit Jalil National Stadium is Malaysia's national stadium, constructed in 1998 to host that year's Commonwealth Games. It was also the venue of the 2001 and 2017 Southeast Asian Games. For the latter event, the stadium and surrounding structures were given a facelift. It is the centre-piece of a larger sports complex, known as KL Sports City. With a seating capacity of 87,000 the stadium is…

spots.name: Endah Parade
spots.desc: Perhaps the largest mall in the vicinity of the National Stadium. Nothing notable for a tourist, but still convenient for one to get groceries from the AEON BIG hypermarket at the lower-ground floor of this shopping mall. Some fast-food outlets inside.

spots.name: The Store Sri Petaling
spots.desc: Another grocery mart in the vicinity, after Endah Parade. Part of a national chain store. However this mart is located in the more bustling part of Sri Petaling, so to speak.

spots.name: Cheras Leisure Mall
spots.desc: Easily spotted along the Kuala Lumpur-Kajang-Seremban federal road, this mall, though not as big as Mid Valley, is still the largest neighbourhood mall serving the locals in Cheras. Connected to the Taman Mutiara metro station, this mall is in operation since 1995. There is a grocery store on the southern wing.

spots.name: Eko Cheras Mall
spots.desc: Located across the KL-Kajang road from Leisure Mall. New mall opened in late-2018, with a grocer store on the ground floor, and the remaining cinema in the area.

spots.name: Cheras Sentral
spots.desc: Despite its name, this mall is not a major public transport hub! Only the Kajang Line MRT (metro) and two buses stop here.

spots.name: Taman Connaught night market
spots.desc: Taman Connaught Chinese pasar malam is the most popular night market in the area, and was dubbed the 'longest Chinese pasar malam in KL'. It's held every Wednesday at the Taman Connaught housing area in Cheras, from dusk until midnight.

spots.name: New Restaurant Ipoh Chicken Rice
spots.desc: Excellent chicken rice, tasty, affordable and in more comfortable atmosphere than Jalan Gasing outlets

spots.name: Uncle Liong
spots.desc: Try some cheap and tasty noodle near Taman OUG Wet Market, Uncle Liong which is inside Restoran Ong Lay, selling Pork Noodle, Spicy Noodle and their Signature Dish-Fish Paste Bitter Gourd Noodle. Other than that there is also a lot of Chinese restaurants around that area. It is located near MCA Seputeh Community Centre.

spots.name: Restaurants along Jalan Radin Anum and Jalan Radin Bagus
spots.desc: A whole street's worth of eateries featuring cuisine from China, Taiwan and South Korea, too many to be listed in detail. As mentioned, this is the more happening part of Sri Petaling.

spots.name: Nanyang Cafe
spots.desc: 2nd floor of Eko Cheras Mall. Check out their wanton mee, sandwiches and Yuenyeung (HK-styled coffee and milk tea mix).

spots.name: Uncle Don's
spots.desc: Western restaurant and bar, attached to the southern wing of Leisure Mall. Do check out their pizzas.

spots.name: Reflexology
spots.desc: Desa Sri Hartamas probably has the largest number of reflexology centres per unit area in KL.

spots.name: Plaza Mont' Kiara Fiesta Nite
spots.desc: A bazaar every Thursday, selling food, clothing, toys, household appliances, etc.

spots.name: Carnaval Churrascaria
spots.desc: Just for meat lovers. The name of this game is meat! Lots of it! Amazing Brazilian meat serviced until you are too full to walk.

spots.name: Bricks & Barrels
spots.desc: Large semi-opened air bar and restaurant with good happy hour promotions. Mix of local office workers along with expat who stay in the area. Be prepared to make reservations during large sporting events. Food specialties include wood fire pizzas and plenty of pork dishes.
spots.price: Before 9PM, drink prices RM 10-20 for a beer and after 9PM, RM 20-30

spots.name: Souled Out
spots.desc: One of the original large restaurants/bars in Sri Hartamas. Always a good time here, drinks and food are of pretty high standards. Note that they do not serve pork here. Large TV and projectors constantly show live sporting events. Be prepared to make reservations for evenings.

spots.name: Garden of Thousand Flowers
spots.desc: Has walking tracks, fountains, pergola, and plenty of flowers and other plants. Nice place to stroll.

spots.name: Melaka Bee Gallery
spots.desc: Offers small exposition explaining how bee farms work. They also sell honey.

spots.name: KFC Ayer Keroh (Drive-Through)
spots.desc: This is fast food restaurant for those who want to try the famous KFC with local menu. The restaurant also served breakfast menu start at 4AM until 11AM daily. If you prefer to eat at somewhere else, the restaurant provide drive-through counter for the convenience. Limited parking spots around the restaurant and sometimes it can be full especially during evening. The restaurant also provide…

spots.name: Muzium Kereta Api Gemas
spots.desc: The old Gemas station is now an open-air museum. Unfortunately, there are no informative descriptions or the like. There is an old locomotive, a crane, a few carriages and a footbridge. Take a few selfies. Your visit will be over in 10 minutes.

spots.name: Phuan
spots.desc: Happy Restoran, about 100 m to the right along the row of shophouses on the first street just outside the train station. The Chinese woman sells all kinds of noodles (soup or fried), rice dishes & drinks (hot & cold) for RM3-4. Food is good & cook when you order. Chicken Rice - Turn left at the first main intersection after leaving the train station then take the first right. This shop is the…

spots.name: Kolej Tuanku Ja'afar
spots.desc: It is a British-style boarding school which was founded in 1991.

spots.name: Staffield Country Resort
spots.desc: It is a 27-hole international standard golf course which opened its doors in 1994. See external link for more details.

spots.name: Wild Junction
spots.desc: - Professional Mountain Guide (all guides are licensed and registered with Ministry of Tourism Malaysia)

spots.name: Bao Sheng Durian Farm
spots.desc: Located about 10 min from the Teluk Bahang Dam, the farm offers a durian buffet (early reservation required) and a variety of tropical fruits during the local fruit & durian season (May - Aug).
spots.price: RM75 includes eating unlimited durians for 2 hr 20 min durian tour (there are 4 sessions daily: 11AM, 1PM, 3PM, 5PM).…

spots.name: Saanen Dairy Goat Farm
spots.desc: Billy goats, nanny goats and kids in a raised and shaded enclosure. Clean with no overpowering smell. Free grass is provided to hand feed them and get as close as you want to pat their backs. The kids run around free and will come up close to you to investigate. The goats will have a go at eating anything in range: umbrellas, shoe laces, bags and hats are all fair game to them. Tasty pasteurised…

spots.name: Titi Kerawang Waterfalls
spots.desc: Situated off the side of the road, near a collection of roadside stalls. To reach the falls, follow the trail beside the bridge to the lower falls. The upper falls, which are more impressive, require you to get off the foot bridge climb over rocks, so be careful and take your time. There is a water pool at the base of the upper falls for a dip. It can be busy during the weekends if coming by bus…

spots.name: Tropical Fruit Farm
spots.desc: 25-acre farm lies in the scenic hills near Balik Pulau. You can view over 200 types of tropical and sub-tropical fruit trees and samples of fresh fruit are available. Highlights include the cinnamon bark cut from a live tree and the miracle berries that can change a sour lime to a sweet taste. A small stall near the entrance sells fresh fruit juice and fruit dishes. You can also enjoy a great…
spots.price: 30-minute guided farm tour (incl. fruit plate & fruit juice) - RM40 for adult and RM30 for children

spots.name: Xuan Wu Temple
spots.desc: A small Chinese temple in Balik Pulau town centre, dedicated to the Taoist deity of the same name. There is a large bell originally cast in 1895.

spots.name: Explore Balik Pulau
spots.desc: A guided bicycle tour run by the local visitors centre, offering a glimpse into the towns, fruit farms, rice paddies and fishing villages of Penang. Don't forget to bring a hat, sunscreen and water as it can get quite hot during the day. Bike rental without a guide is also available, but the tour is excellent for first timers to Balik Pulau.
spots.price: Bike hire RM20; tour with bike hire RM30

spots.name: Balik Pulau Market
spots.desc: A market area to replace the old market of Balik Pulau. The building houses a wet and dry market, selling local produce along with everything under the sun.

spots.name: Ghee Hup Nutmeg Factory
spots.desc: Small shop/stall selling nutmeg products. Besides, owner gives free 5-minute speech explaining how nutmegs are grown, and gives you a free welcome nutmeg drink.

spots.name: Nan Guang Kopitiam
spots.desc: This small coffeeshop serves up the well sought after Assam Laksa (also known simply as Balik Pulau laksa), along with the Lemak Laksa variation, which has a touch of coconut milk to cut through the sourness.

spots.name: Penang Bird Park
spots.desc: A small bird park located on the mainland (Seberang Perai) about 10 min from the Penang Bridge. Take a walk under nice shady trees and view dozens of kinds of birds including ostriches, sea eagles, peafowls, hornbills, flamingos, macaws, and grey parrots. There are also two walk-through aviaries and a fish pond. Some of the enclosures do need a touch of paint, but kids should love this place.

spots.name: Pacific Megamall
spots.desc: the biggest shopping mall in the district, 2nd is the JUSCO Bandar Perda located in Bukit Mertajam.

spots.name: Sunway Carnival
spots.desc: a stylish 4-storey shopping mall strategically located within the town center of Seberang Jaya. Parkson Departmental Store and Giant Hypermarket are both the anchor tenants. With a total of 161 specialty outlets ranging from international to regional retailers, and even an amusement centre.

spots.name: Pulau Aman
spots.desc: A small island between the first Penang Bridge and the new bridge. The ferry is at Batu Kawan's Batu Musang Jetty (you need own transport to get there- 45 min drive from Georgetown). The 5min boat trip costs RM6 for a return journey. M-F the boat departs Batu Musang for Pulau Aman at 10:00, 13:00, 16:00 and 19:00. The trip from Pulau Aman for Bukit Tambun at 08:00, 12:00, 15:00 and 18:00. On…

spots.name: University Kebangsaan Malaysia
spots.desc: National University of Malaysia, also houses a restricted natural forest reserve.

spots.name: Taman Tasik Cempaka
spots.desc: A well maintained recreation park surrounding a man-made river-lake. Equipped with jogging track, reflexology track, small football/soccer field and gazebos, it is suitable for a leisurely stroll for families as well as after-work sporting activities.

spots.name: PKNS Complex
spots.desc: Shopping mall with supermarket, fastfood and shops with varieties of local goods.

spots.name: Warta Mall
spots.desc: Shopping mall with supermarket and various shopping stalls selling local products and goods.

spots.name: Farmer's Market 1
spots.desc: Every Thursday. Fresh groceries, affordable foods and goodies.
spots.addr: Seksyen 16, near Shell station & PKNS flat houses

spots.name: Farmer's Market 2
spots.desc: Every Sunday. Fresh groceries, affordable foods and goodies.
spots.addr: In front of PKNS shopping mall

spots.name: Bangi Kopitiam
spots.desc: Popular spot for coffee, teh tarik and toast bread, albeit a bit pricey.

spots.name: McDonald's
spots.desc: Two McDonald's outlets, including a Drive-Thru next to the Kompleks PKNS

spots.name: Multi-Rich Pitaya Dragon Fruit Farm
spots.desc: Pay a visit to the farm and observe how dragon fruit is planted. Purchase the fruit and side products of the fruits such as jam or drink.
